addy-skill.text: Markdown-first engineering workflow. Copy the complete skill folder; inspect repo-level references and other named skills. Shared checklists sit outside individual folders, so copy needed checklists and rewrite ../../references paths. Most workflows transfer across agents; browser-testing requires Chrome DevTools MCP, and delegation or source lookup steps need available equivalents. Read examples against the project stack; do not assume TypeScript. Inspect the source LICENSE.

matt-skill.text: Promoted composable workflow. Copy the whole skill folder, including adjacent Markdown, scripts, and agents/openai.yaml where present. Many invoke sibling skills through the Skill tool. Engineering flows may assume issue-tracker, triage, glossary, and ADR configuration from setup-matt-pocock-skills. Adapt these to existing project conventions. Preserve intentional user-only invocation; inspect disable-model-invocation and allow_implicit_invocation rather than enabling everything automatically.

pstack-skill.text: Canonical Cursor source. Copy the complete skill folder and recursively inspect named sibling skills, principle skills, agents, references, scripts, and playbooks. For Claude Code, inspect the generated counterpart under repos/cursor-plugins/harness/pstack/claude-code before selecting the version to copy; retain its adapter. Codex needs tool, delegation, model, path, and invocation adaptation against its actual session capabilities. This is not a drop-in cross-agent installation.

cursor-workflow.text: Cursor-origin workflow or persona. Inspect its whole folder and manifest for invoked agents, commands, rules, hooks, scripts, and services. Translate Cursor tool names and environment assumptions to the actual consuming agent. Delegation or model choices are optional capabilities to assess, not installation prerequisites to impose on every project. Keep existing approval and Git rules.

integration.text: Service integration bundle. Inspect README, manifest, mcp.json where present, rules, skills, and LICENSE. Copy only needed configuration and guidance; adapt to the consuming client schema. Requires the actual service, permissions, credentials or OAuth flow, and a supported MCP transport. Client/backend-managed auth and placeholders do not necessarily transfer to Claude Code or Codex; resolve them explicitly. Catalog inclusion does not verify live endpoints, access, or production maturity.

source-tooling.text: Source-specific maintenance, validation, evaluation, or packaging material. Inspect scripts and local imports together with relevant manifests, fixtures, schemas, and source instructions. Adapt assumptions about directory layout and naming. Evaluation agents may spend tokens; installers, linkers, hooks, and generators may write files. Copying is allowed under project rules; running them requires inspection and the normal project permissions. Root agent instructions are maintenance context, not project starter templates.

reference.text: Reusable checklist, persona, command, or documentation reference. Read the complete source and its links. Select the relevant portions, retain attribution, adapt paths and tooling, and reconcile its policies with the consuming project. A command or persona may invoke sibling skills and require supporting references; it is not necessarily standalone.

project-toolkit-tool.text: Independently copyable tool folder. Copy its complete contents, including ORIGIN.md/ORIGIN.json, notices and sibling imports. Read the local README for command/configuration, exit/completeness and mutation contracts. Most tools use Python 3.10+ standard library; PHP, Bash/Git, SQLite FTS5 and service/client prerequisites are component-specific. No installation, credentials, network call or hook activation transfers with a copy. Tests use fixtures; live services and agent-runtime behavior are not certified.

project-toolkit-skill.text: Reusable workflow adapted from local project practice. Copy the complete skill folder with its origin/notices and the explicitly listed tool/reference bundles; preserve the relative skills/tools/references layout or rewrite links after relocation. Replace client-specific tools with available equivalents. Keep the consumer's authorization, testing, Git and shipping rules; source approvals/model defaults do not transfer.

project-toolkit-framework.text: Version-specific PHP/Laravel reference skill. Copy the whole folder, including rules/references and upstream licence/origin. Check the actual installed package/version against provenance and adapt documentation/MCP lookup to available tools or official docs. Consumer conventions and permissions govern. These are static reference adaptations; framework APIs and installed client behavior were not exercised end to end.

project-toolkit-reference.text: Reusable operational checklist or template derived from dated project practice. Copy the Markdown plus adjacent origin files. Keep source attribution and applicable licences, and adapt environment, workload and approval assumptions. The reference does not authorize executing source infrastructure/provisioning commands.

project-toolkit-maintenance.text: Collection-specific maintenance and validation. Use in an intact toolkit checkout, or copy the full listed context to adapt the checker. This is not an application starter or policy installer. Requires Python, Git, Bash and PHP for all checks; fixture tests do not require paid models, live services or database/daemon access. Preserve origin records and review changes before refreshing hashes.

cut-the-fluff.text: Warehouse-owned portable skill; copy the entire package with references, Python helpers, schemas, tests, provenance and notices. Python 3.11+ standard library; POSIX required only for approved mutation. WSL drvfs changes require Linux-hosted private state. Inventory loading profiles remain documentation-based with synthetic compatibility tests: newer numeric Claude versions or later Codex docs snapshots retain loading expectations at low confidence with a newer_version gap; older/unparseable versions and Codex binary versions have unknown loading. Claude transcript analysis and read-only pilots were exercised on real stores; unresolved dynamic file accesses qualify file-read coverage separately. Codex adapter: validated on 1 rollout, metadata shapes only; opaque outcomes and unattributable native file changes keep it partial. Twelve fresh restricted Claude sessions preserve fixture answers/discovery while routed-task API input increases; native startup/skill activation and general token savings remain unvalidated. Read the validation/runtime/change contracts. Explicit audit scope and exact user approval are required for real-project changes. No agent launcher, hooks, global installation, telemetry or service dependency.

ponytail-skill.text: Single-file lazy-senior-developer skills (YAGNI, standard library first, one-line caveat at the end of each reply). Copy the whole skill folder; each is one SKILL.md with no scripts or sibling-skill invocations, but ponytail-help lists the other five and the /ponytail level switch (lite/full/ultra) only persists when the Claude/Codex hooks are installed, so otherwise level changes last for the session at most. ponytail-gain prints benchmark figures from the source's benchmarks/results folder; the figures are the vendor's own, not a measurement of the consuming project. The policy of minimal diffs and small asserted self-checks can conflict with a project's own testing or architecture rules: pick one coherent policy. Inspect the source LICENSE (MIT) and keep attribution.

ponytail-host-adapter.text: Host-specific distribution adapters around the canonical skills. Hooks are Node.js (CommonJS, standard library only) and need CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT or an equivalent root variable, path rewrites after relocation, and explicit user approval before being enabled. The Claude/Codex hooks write a mode flag under the agent config directory and may edit statusline settings. The optional band ledger (claude-band.json, hooks/band, ponytail-band-import.js) writes a per-project CSV under ~/.config/ponytail and can post each turn's row to a user-configured webhook: leave it out unless wanted and approved. Plugin manifests and marketplace files describe upstream installation and publishing; read them as reference, do not install or publish from the warehouse.

routes.task: Clarify requirements
routes.choice: Compare interview style, persistence of glossary/ADRs, and required sibling skills.

routes.choice: Addy provides a staged lifecycle. Matt synthesizes existing discussion and may publish to a configured tracker.

routes.choice: Choose a focused interface reference or a fuller design process; formal tooling requires runtime setup.

routes.task: Implement or simplify
routes.choice: Inspect test/review dependencies and commit policy before adopting an implementation flow.

routes.task: Choose a testing policy
routes.choice: These disagree on testing scope, user checkpoints, and refactoring. Choose a coherent policy before mixing.

routes.task: Verify browser, CLI, or application behavior
routes.choice: Match the driver to the app. A reusable harness needs app-specific launch, fixtures, evidence, and cleanup.

routes.task: Diagnose bugs or performance
routes.choice: Prefer a bounded reproduction and measured evidence; inspect scripts and environment requirements.

routes.task: Review code, security, or readiness
routes.choice: Choose lightweight checks or deeper multi-agent review according to project needs and available tools.

routes.task: Fix CI, ship, or maintain
routes.choice: Keep verification separate from permission to push, merge, deploy, or send messages.

routes.task: Manage context, handoffs, and learned practices
routes.choice: Choose persistent project knowledge versus a session handoff; inspect transcript and output-location assumptions.

routes.task: Connect a service or automate an integration
routes.choice: Browse Integrations for all eligible bundles. Connection metadata is a reference, not proof that authentication transfers.

routes.task: Validate or evaluate reusable skills
routes.choice: Adapt structural/routing validators and fixtures to the catalog being tested; behavioral runs cost agent tokens.

routes.task: Read compact test, scan and CI evidence
routes.choice: Choose a report reader or configured service adapter. Missing or incomplete input is unavailable evidence; conversion success and CI green do not authorize merge or prove deployment.

routes.task: Navigate code and control context cost
routes.choice: Choose deterministic navigation/editing helpers first. Explicitly scope transcript/index access; the lexical subset invokes no models and claims no benchmark gain for another workload.

routes.task: Run recoverable worktrees and protect staged work
routes.choice: Use a journalled worktree core with reviewed project setup/teardown adapters. Preserve index/worktree identity before fixers; Laravel database operations are optional stack-specific mutations.

routes.task: Track project gates and specification drift
routes.choice: Use local configurable state and checks rather than importing product gates or a whole scaffold. Human approval records are not authenticated by a name string.

routes.task: Generate PHP quality tool configuration
routes.choice: Generating configs does not install or run scanners; match the installed tool versions.

routes.task: Validate UX labs and adversarial fixture evidence
routes.choice: Separate automated consistency and positive controls from actual human acceptance. No unfinished product labs, hostile corpora or draft product schemas are copied.

routes.task: Review origins before a manual toolkit update
routes.choice: Select local source roots explicitly and review file-level changes before adapting. The toolkit never fetches or syncs sources automatically.

routes.task: Reduce agent context overhead while preserving capability discovery
routes.choice: Use the scoped report and approved-change workflow; retain rare workflows and review behavior evidence separately from byte estimates.

routes.task: Keep agent changes minimal and flag deferred shortcuts
routes.choice: Always-on YAGNI policy with a deferred-shortcut ledger. It competes with the simplify entries (addy-code-simplification, cursor-pstack-no-comments) and with project test or architecture policies; choose one policy and avoid stacking them.

assets.name: api-and-interface-design
assets.description: Guides stable API and interface design. Use when designing APIs, module boundaries, or any public interface. Use when creating REST or GraphQL endpoints, defining type contracts between modules, or establishing boundaries between frontend and backend.

assets.name: browser-testing-with-devtools
assets.description: Tests in real browsers via Chrome DevTools MCP. Use when building or debugging anything that runs in a browser. Use when you need to inspect the DOM, capture console errors, analyze network requests, profile performance, or verify visual output with real runtime data. Requires the chrome-devtools MCP server to be configured.
assets.notes: Requires configured Chrome DevTools MCP; adapt to another browser driver only with equivalent runtime evidence.

assets.name: ci-cd-and-automation
assets.description: Automates CI/CD pipeline setup. Use when setting up or modifying build and deployment pipelines. Use when you need to automate quality gates, configure test runners in CI, or establish deployment strategies.

assets.name: code-review-and-quality
assets.description: Conducts multi-axis code review. Use before merging any change. Use when reviewing code written by yourself, another agent, or a human. Use when you need to assess code quality across multiple dimensions before it enters the main branch. Use when asked to review a diff or a pull request, even when the diff is pasted inline.

assets.name: code-simplification
assets.description: Simplifies code for clarity. Use when refactoring code for clarity without changing behavior. Use when code works but is harder to read, maintain, or extend than it should be. Use when reviewing code that has accumulated unnecessary complexity. Use when asked to simplify, clean up, or reduce the nesting of a function or module that already works, even when the code is pasted inline and nothing else needs to change.

assets.name: constraint-driven-development
assets.description: Establishes a project's quality bar as a written contract and stops agents quietly lowering it. Interviews the user on which dimensions matter, supplies sane default thresholds when they have no number in mind, records everything in CONSTRAINTS.md, and watches the diff for a weakened bar — new @ts-ignore or eslint-disable suppressions, skipped or deleted tests, assertions stripped out, unimplemented stubs, thresholds edited down. Use when no quality bar is written down, when the user says "set up constraints" or "define our standards", when the user wants dimensions they care about — accessibility, web performance, coverage — set up as enforced constraints, when an agent keeps silencing checks or skipping tests to get to green, when you need a coverage or performance threshold and don't know what number to pick, or when an agent writes more code than anyone will read.

assets.name: context-engineering
assets.description: Optimizes agent context setup. Use when starting a new session, when agent output quality degrades, when switching between tasks, or when you need to configure rules files and context for a project.

assets.name: debugging-and-error-recovery
assets.description: Guides systematic root-cause debugging. Use when tests fail, builds break, something that worked yesterday broke, behavior doesn't match expectations, or you encounter any unexpected error. Use when you need to figure out what broke and why — a systematic approach to finding and fixing the root cause rather than guessing.

assets.name: deprecation-and-migration
assets.description: Manages deprecation and migration. Use when removing old systems, APIs, or features. Use when migrating users from one implementation to another. Use when migrating a database schema in production, such as renaming or dropping a column without downtime (expand/contract). Use when deciding whether to maintain or sunset existing code.

assets.name: documentation-and-adrs
assets.description: Records decisions and documentation. Use when you need to document an architecture decision (ADR) or the reasoning behind a design choice, when changing public APIs, shipping features, or when you need to record context that future engineers and agents will need to understand the codebase.

assets.name: doubt-driven-development
assets.description: Subjects every non-trivial decision to a fresh-context adversarial review before it stands. Use when you want every assumption cross-examined before proceeding, when stress-testing a plan for hidden failure modes, when correctness matters more than speed, when working in unfamiliar code, when stakes are high (production auth, security-sensitive logic, a high-stakes migration, irreversible operations), or any time a confident output would be cheaper to verify now than to debug later.

assets.name: frontend-ui-engineering
assets.description: Builds production-quality, accessible, responsive user-facing UIs. Use when building or modifying interfaces and pages, creating components, implementing layouts, meeting WCAG accessibility requirements, managing state, or when the output needs to look and feel production-quality rather than AI-generated.

assets.name: git-workflow-and-versioning
assets.description: Structures git workflow practices. Use when making any code change. Use when committing, branching, resolving conflicts, splitting uncommitted work in a messy working tree into clean atomic commits, opening or reviewing a pull request (PR), pushing to a remote, or when you need to organize work across multiple parallel streams. Use when cutting a release, choosing a semantic version bump, tagging, or writing a changelog. Use when asked to write a commit message or a changelog entry for a change, or to split a change into commits, even when the diff is pasted inline and the message seems easy to write from it.

assets.name: idea-refine
assets.description: Refines raw ideas into sharp, actionable concepts through structured divergent and convergent thinking. Use when an idea is still vague, when you need to stress-test assumptions before committing to a plan, or when you want to expand options before converging on one. Triggers on "ideate", "refine this idea", or "stress-test my plan".

assets.name: incremental-implementation
assets.description: Delivers changes incrementally in thin, verifiable slices. Use when implementing any feature or change that touches more than one file, or when picking up the next task from a plan. Use when rolling a change out behind a feature flag, when you're about to write a large amount of code at once, or when a task feels too big to land in one step.

assets.name: interview-me
assets.description: Extracts what the user actually wants instead of what they think they should want. Achieves this through one-question-at-a-time interview until ~95% confidence about the underlying intent. Use when an ask is underspecified ("build me X" without "for whom" or "why now"), when the user explicitly invokes ("interview me", "grill me", "are we sure?", "stress-test my thinking"), or when you catch yourself silently filling in ambiguous requirements before any plan, spec, or code exists.

assets.name: observability-and-instrumentation
assets.description: Instruments code so production behavior is visible and diagnosable. Use when adding logging, metrics, tracing, or alerting. Use when shipping any feature that runs in production and you need evidence it works. Use when production issues are reported but you can't tell what happened from the available data.

assets.name: performance-optimization
assets.description: Optimizes application performance across frontend, backend, queries, and databases. Use when performance requirements exist, when you suspect performance regressions, when Core Web Vitals or load times need improvement, when N+1 query patterns need fixing, or when profiling reveals bottlenecks.

assets.name: planning-and-task-breakdown
assets.description: Breaks work into ordered tasks. Use when you have a spec or clear requirements and need to break work into implementable tasks. Use when a task feels too large to start, when you need to estimate scope, or when parallel work is possible.

assets.name: security-and-hardening
assets.description: Hardens code against vulnerabilities. Use when auditing an input handler for vulnerabilities, when handling user input, authentication, data storage, or external integrations, or when checking a login flow is safe against the OWASP Top Ten. Use when building any feature that accepts untrusted data, manages user sessions or session cookies, or interacts with third-party services. Use when auditing dependencies for known vulnerabilities, triaging package-manager audit findings, or assessing supply-chain risk in a new package. Use when personal data or privacy compliance (GDPR, CCPA) is involved.

assets.name: shipping-and-launch
assets.description: Prepares production launches. Use when preparing to deploy to production, or when asking what needs to be in place before shipping. Use when you need a pre-launch checklist, when setting up monitoring, when planning a staged rollout, or when you need a rollback strategy.

assets.name: source-driven-development
assets.description: Grounds every implementation decision in official documentation. Use when you want to verify an approach against the official docs before implementing it, or when you want authoritative, source-cited code free from outdated patterns. Use when building with any framework or library where correctness matters.

assets.name: spec-driven-development
assets.description: Creates specs before coding. Use when starting a new project, feature, or significant change and no specification exists yet. Use when drafting a PRD or requirements document with objectives and scope, or when requirements are unclear, ambiguous, or only exist as a vague idea. Use when a single requirement spans several independently testable capabilities and needs decomposing into a capability map of modules before specifying.

assets.name: test-driven-development
assets.description: Drives development with tests using the red-green-refactor loop. Use when implementing any logic, fixing any bug, or changing any behavior. Use when you need to prove that code works, when a bug report arrives, or when you're about to modify existing functionality. Use when asked to add tests to a function, fix a bug in it or change its behavior, even when the code is pasted inline and the request does not mention tests.
assets.notes: Broad behavioral TDD with red-green-refactor and project-stack discovery; exempts documentation and static configuration changes.

assets.name: using-agent-skills
assets.description: Discovers and invokes agent skills. Use when starting a session, or when you need to decide which skill or workflow applies to the piece of work at hand. This is the meta-skill that governs how all other skills are discovered and invoked.

assets.name: ask-matt
assets.description: Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo.

assets.name: code-review
assets.description: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".

assets.name: codebase-design
assets.description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.

assets.name: diagnosing-bugs
assets.description: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.

assets.name: domain-modeling
assets.description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a GLOSSARY.md, or recording or editing an ADR.

assets.name: grill-with-docs
assets.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go.
assets.notes: Invokes grilling and domain-modeling; may create glossary and ADR artifacts.

assets.name: implement
assets.description: Implement a piece of work based on a spec or set of tickets.
assets.notes: Invokes tdd and code-review, assumes a spec/tickets, and commits on the current branch. Reconcile commit behavior with the consuming project.

assets.name: implement-spec
assets.description: Implement the result of /to-spec and /to-tickets in code.
assets.notes: Companion implementation flow for to-spec/to-tickets; inspect both skill dependencies and tracker configuration.

assets.name: improve-codebase-architecture
assets.description: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick.

assets.name: pr
assets.description: Use when writing a PR body.

assets.name: prototype
assets.description: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.

assets.name: research
assets.description: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.

assets.name: retro
assets.description: Conduct a retrospective on a coding session.

assets.name: setup-matt-pocock-skills
assets.description: Configure this repo for the engineering skills: set up its issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, and domain doc layout. Run once before first use of the other engineering skills.
assets.notes: Writes project-specific tracker, triage, and domain-document configuration. Adapt to existing conventions rather than replacing them.

assets.name: tdd
assets.description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
assets.notes: Requires user agreement on public testing seams before tests; refactoring belongs to review, outside its red-green loop. Depends on adjacent tests.md/mocking.md and may invoke codebase-design.

assets.name: to-spec
assets.description: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker: no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed.

assets.name: to-tickets
assets.description: Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, published to the configured tracker (edges as text in one file per ticket locally, or native blocking links on a real tracker).

assets.name: triage
assets.description: Move issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles, categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs.

assets.name: wayfinder
assets.description: Plan a huge chunk of work (more than one agent session can hold) as a shared map of decision tickets on your issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.

assets.name: wizard
assets.description: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.

assets.name: grill-me
assets.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design.
assets.notes: Thin entry point that invokes grilling. Copy/adapt that sibling as well.

assets.name: grilling
assets.description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.

assets.name: handoff
assets.description: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up.
assets.notes: Writes to the OS temporary directory and references existing artifacts rather than duplicating them. Adjust retention if the receiving agent is on another machine.

assets.name: teach
assets.description: Teach the user a new skill or concept, within this workspace.

assets.name: to-questionnaire
assets.description: Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in.

assets.name: wait-what
assets.description: Stop. That last message did not land: re-pitch it.

assets.name: writing-for-agents
assets.description: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.

assets.name: advisor
assets.description: Advisor mode. Consult a stronger (or different) model at key checkpoints: before major decisions, when stuck on an error, and before declaring a task done. Use when the user types /advisor, asks to turn the advisor on or off, picks an advisor model, or explicitly asks for a second opinion from a stronger or different model. Never enable it on your own.

assets.name: check-agent-compatibility
assets.description: Run the full repository compatibility pass: scanner score, startup path, validation loop, and docs reliability.

assets.name: cli-for-agents
assets.description: Designs or reviews CLIs so coding agents can run them reliably: non-interactive flags, layered --help with examples, stdin/pipelines, fast actionable errors, idempotency, dry-run, and predictable structure. Use when building a CLI, adding commands, writing --help, or when the user mentions agents, terminals, or automation-friendly CLIs.

assets.notes: Thin orchestrator depending on agents-memory-updater and transcript access; hook uses Bun and Cursor transcript conventions.

assets.name: review-plugin-submission
assets.description: Audit a Cursor plugin for marketplace readiness. Use when validating manifests, component metadata, discovery paths, and submission quality before publishing.

assets.name: cursor-sdk

Use this skill whenever the user mentions integrating, installing, or writing code against the Cursor SDK; whenever they say `Agent.create`, `Agent.prompt`, `Agent.resume`, `agent.send`, `run.stream`, `CursorAgentError`, or `@cursor/sdk`; whenever they ask to run Cursor agents programmatically from a script, CI/CD pipeline, GitHub Action, backend service, or any other code that isn't the Cursor IDE itself; and whenever they want to pick between local and cloud runtime, configure MCP servers for an SDK agent, or handle streaming, cancellation, or errors from an SDK agent. assets.description: Run compile and type-check commands and report failures

assets.name: control-cli

assets.name: control-ui
assets.description: Build or adapt a local browser/CDP harness to drive and inspect a web, IDE, or Electron UI. Use for local UI verification, screenshots, accessibility snapshots, perf profiles, visual diffs, or reproducing UI bugs.

assets.name: deslop
assets.description: Remove AI-generated code slop and clean up code style

assets.name: fix-ci
assets.description: Find failing PR checks, inspect logs or external check links, and apply focused fixes
assets.notes: Its workflow pushes changes while iterating. Apply the consuming project approval rules before any push.

assets.name: fix-merge-conflicts
assets.description: Resolve merge conflicts non-interactively, validate build and tests, and finalize conflict resolution

assets.name: get-pr-comments
assets.description: Fetch and summarize review comments from the active pull request

assets.name: loop-on-ci
assets.description: Monitor PR checks and fix failures until green. Uses gh pr checks as the source of truth for PR-attached checks.

assets.name: make-pr-easy-to-review
assets.description: Prepare PRs for review by cleaning noisy history, improving PR descriptions, and adding reviewer guidance without changing code behavior. Use for "make this easy to review", "tidy this PR", "clean up commits", or "annotate the diff".

assets.name: run-smoke-tests

assets.name: thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review
assets.description: Run an extremely strict maintainability review for abstraction quality, giant files, and spaghetti-condition growth. Use for a thermo-nuclear code quality review, thermonuclear review, deep code quality audit, or especially harsh maintainability review.

assets.name: verify-this

assets.name: principle-encode-lessons-in-structure

assets.name: principle-exhaust-the-design-space
assets.description: Apply when facing a novel UI interaction or architectural decision with no precedent in the codebase. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare side by side before committing.

assets.name: principle-experience-first
assets.description: Apply when product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs come up. Choose user delight over implementation convenience; ship fewer polished features over more rough ones.

assets.name: principle-explain-the-number
assets.description: Apply before you measure, and before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured: a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result. Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.

assets.name: principle-fix-root-causes
assets.description: Apply when debugging. Trace each symptom back to the first place the system went wrong and fix it there. A guard is a fix only when the state it handles is legitimate.

assets.name: principle-foundational-thinking
assets.description: Apply before writing logic: choosing core types and data structures, sequencing scaffold-vs-feature work, asking what concurrent actors share. Get the data structures right so downstream code becomes obvious.

assets.name: principle-guard-the-context-window
assets.description: Apply when context is filling up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents; keep summaries in the main thread, not raw payloads.

assets.name: principle-laziness-protocol
assets.description: Apply when refactoring, evaluating diff size, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.

assets.name: principle-make-operations-idempotent
assets.description: Apply when designing commands, lifecycle steps, or processing loops that run amid crashes, restarts, and retries. Converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs.

assets.name: principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis
assets.description: Apply when introducing a new internal API while old callers still exist. Migrate callers and delete the old API in the same wave instead of preserving compatibility layers.

assets.name: principle-minimize-reader-load
assets.description: Apply when reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers between question and answer, and hidden state in the reader's head; collapse one-caller wrappers and shrink mutable scope.

assets.name: principle-model-the-domain
assets.description: Apply when writing stateful logic, or when code branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files.

assets.name: principle-never-block-on-the-human
assets.description: Apply when tempted to ask 'should I do X?' on reversible work.

assets.name: principle-outcome-oriented-execution
assets.description: Apply during planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture; don't preserve smooth intermediate states with throwaway compatibility code.

assets.name: principle-prove-it-works
assets.description: Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'

assets.name: principle-redesign-from-first-principles
assets.description: Apply when integrating a new requirement into an existing design.

assets.name: principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state
assets.description: Apply when concurrent actors might write to the same file, branch, key, or state object. Eliminate the sharing first; serialize structurally only when one shared writer is a real invariant.

assets.name: principle-sequence-verifiable-units

assets.name: principle-subtract-before-you-add

assets.name: principle-test-behavior-not-implementation

assets.name: principle-type-system-discipline
